doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Afternoon in Paris session with Sonny Stitt
summary: Baker asks about a Savoy date with John Lewis and Stitt; Johnson only remembers the tunes.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Let me ask you about one other thing while you’re here [in this time period]: the very first recording of Afternoon in Paris with Sonny Stitt, because Sonny played tenor on that. It was you and John Lewis and Sonny Stitt. I remember now, going back, it was a very square version the way they played the head [the melody] at that time, considering what it was going to be a little later on. I wondered if you remembered much about the date because the two Sonnys, Sonny Stitt on Afternoon in Paris. I’m trying to think. It seems like there might have been Elora or one of those tunes on the other side of it. I bought it. I think it was on Savoy Records. I don’t remember. It was a purple record.

Yeah, and I remember it might have been Elora. [Baker sings the first measures of Elora.] Anyway, Sonny Stitt. I was just wondering if you recollect much there. I know he would use him later on that television show.

Yeah, it's hazy, David, I don’t really remember much about that situation. I remember that it happened, and I remember those tunes, of course – Elora and what was the other thing you mentioned? Afternoon in Paris.
Yeah. [Johnson sings the opening measures of Afternoon in Paris.]
I don’t remember much about the chemistry or the environment of the situation.
